questions.question: What is the most appropriate way to begin a weight-related discussion?
choices: Ask permission and connect the discussion to the patient’s health goals
Assume the patient wants weight loss discussed at every visit
Use shame to improve adherence
Avoid assessing metabolic risk
questions.explanation: Permission-based, person-first communication improves trust and helps the patient define meaningful goals. Weight stigma can cause harm and delay care.

questions.question: Which statement best describes obesity?
choices: A complex chronic disease influenced by biology, medicines, sleep, mental health, environment, and social context
A condition caused only by personal willpower
A diagnosis that rules out all other causes of symptoms
A reason to skip a focused examination
questions.explanation: Obesity is multifactorial. FNP care should assess biology, behavior, medications, access, function, and complications without blame.

questions.question: Which feature requires focused assessment rather than automatic praise for weight loss?
choices: Rapid unintentional loss with early satiety and dark stools
Improved mobility after a planned activity program
Stable weight with better sleep
A patient requesting nutrition support
questions.explanation: Unintentional weight loss with systemic or GI warning symptoms can indicate serious disease and needs diagnostic evaluation.

questions.question: What should be included in a metabolic-health assessment?
choices: Weight trajectory, BP, glucose, lipids, sleep, function, medicines, eating pattern, mental health, and access
Only BMI
Only calorie intake
Only family history
questions.explanation: A full assessment identifies cardiometabolic risk, drivers, complications, safety concerns, and practical treatment options.

questions.question: Why should an FNP screen for eating-disorder symptoms in a patient in a larger body?
choices: Eating disorders can occur at any body size and restrictive plans may worsen risk
Only underweight people can have eating disorders
It is unrelated to medication safety
Screening is unnecessary if the patient requests weight loss
questions.explanation: Binge eating, purging, restrictive eating, and body-image distress can create medical and psychiatric risk regardless of body size.

questions.question: Before starting an anti-obesity medication, what is essential?
choices: Review indication, contraindications, safety, interactions, pregnancy potential, access, and follow-up capacity
Promise a specific amount of weight loss
Ignore gastrointestinal and mental-health history
Use the same regimen for every patient
questions.explanation: Medication selection is individualized. It requires current product information, patient-specific risk assessment, counseling, and longitudinal monitoring.

questions.question: Which outcome can represent meaningful success in obesity care?
choices: Improved sleep, mobility, blood pressure, glucose, or quality of life aligned with the patient’s goals
Only a number on the scale
No need for continued follow-up after any loss
Never discussing medication or referral
questions.explanation: Health outcomes are broader than scale weight. Patient-defined goals and metabolic, functional, and psychosocial improvements all matter.

questions.question: What is the best description of metabolic or bariatric surgery care?
choices: A longitudinal treatment pathway requiring pre- and postoperative nutrition, mental-health, medication, and follow-up planning
A one-time intervention that ends medical care
A treatment that can be discussed without pregnancy or nutrition context
A substitute for all primary care
questions.explanation: Surgery can be effective for selected patients, but it requires comprehensive assessment, preparation, long-term monitoring, and coordinated care.

questions.question: A patient has loud snoring, daytime somnolence, hypertension, and obesity. What contributor should be assessed?
choices: Obstructive sleep apnea
A harmless preference for sleeping late
Only calorie intake
A normal lipid panel
questions.explanation: Sleep-disordered breathing can affect cardiometabolic health, blood pressure, fatigue, mood, and treatment feasibility.

questions.question: Which response avoids diagnostic overshadowing?
choices: Evaluate a patient’s new chest pain or abdominal pain with the same appropriate differential used for any patient
Assume all symptoms are caused by body size
Delay assessment until weight changes
Avoid asking about red flags
questions.explanation: Weight should never replace clinical reasoning. New symptoms deserve an appropriate differential, examination, and disposition assessment.
